hypotheses.name: Bayesian hierarchical-shrinkage latent linear operator
hypotheses.scientific_question: Does replacing a deterministic least-squares latent linear operator A with a Bayesian posterior over A — using hierarchical shrinkage priors on per-POD-mode eigenvalue magnitudes — produce better calibrated long-horizon predictive distributions and a stratified (energy-aware) posterior uncertainty on the same latent representation?
hypotheses.mechanism: Treat the latent transition z_{t+1} = A z_t + ε as a Bayesian linear regression. Instead of a single point-estimate A, place a hierarchical Laplace prior on each eigenvalue λ_i(A) with scale b_i that decreases with POD mode energy. Low-energy eigenvalues (poorly identified from data) are shrunk toward zero; high-energy eigenvalues are estimated aggressively. Propagate the full posterior predictive distribution N(A z_t, σ² I + z_t^T Σ_A z_t I) rather than only the mean, so scoring can use log predictive density and continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) instead of plain MSE.
hypotheses.mathematical_form: Observation model: z_{t+1} = A z_t + ε, ε ~ N(0, σ² I), A ∈ R^{52×52}. Eigendecompose A = V Λ V^{-1}. Prior: p(Λ) = ∏_i Laplace(λ_i | 0, b_i), b_i = b_0 · exp(-α · i / 52), α ≥ 0. Posterior: p(A|Σ) approximated by Laplace/VI. Predictive: p(z_{t+1} | z_t, Σ) ≈ ∫ N(z_{t+1}; A z_t, σ² I) p(A|Σ) dA. Metrics: log predictive density, CRPS at horizons 1, 5, 20; per-mode posterior marginal std of λ_i.
hypotheses.motivation: POD latent spaces typically have heavy-tailed eigenvalue spectra: a few high-energy modes dominate, and the long tail is poorly constrained by the data. A deterministic ridge A overfits the tail and gives overconfident predictions there. A hierarchical Bayesian operator quantifies this structurally and is the natural scientific upgrade of the deterministic linear-operator family that BOOTSTRAP_H1 used (and which produced only an inconclusive schema-mismatch verdict, not a scientific falsification).
hypotheses.explanation_of_previous_failure: BOOTSTRAP_H1's deterministic regime-dependent operator finished without comparable metrics; that was a measurement problem, not a scientific refutation. C002_H01 (symplectic) and C002_H02 (exogenous-parameter-conditioned) tried richer operator priors but required unavailable inputs and/or a pipeline change. C003_H01 keeps the linear-operator family but adds a probabilistic wrapper that uses only latent_state and latent_history and requires no physical-field inputs — it should pass the data-policy validator that rejected C002_H03.
hypotheses.distinguishing_prediction: If the hierarchical-shrinkage mechanism is correct: (a) per-mode posterior std of λ_i decreases monotonically with POD mode energy index i; (b) log predictive density on development_validation exceeds the deterministic ridge baseline, and the gap grows with horizon (because predictive variance properly reflects tail uncertainty); (c) the 95% predictive intervals cover ~95% of held-out transitions at the nominal level.
hypotheses.minimum_experiment: Train on development_train with α ∈ {0, 2, 4} and b_0 ∈ {0.1, 1.0, 10.0}. Evaluate on development_validation: 1-step log predictive density, 20-step rolling CRPS, per-mode posterior std of λ_i, calibration curve of predictive intervals. Use latent_dim=52 explicitly in the contract; call AlgorithmAgent.run(research_dir=..., output_dir=...) to avoid the C001_* missing-args failure; restrict representation.normalization to development_train and development_validation to avoid the C002_H03 final-test-access detection. Falsification criterion: if no (α, b_0) setting produces log predictive density above the deterministic ridge baseline AND per-mode posterior std is not stratified by mode energy (i.e., the prior is being ignored), the hierarchical-shrinkage mechanism is rejected.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_true: Per-mode λ_i posterior std is a clearly decreasing function of mode index; log predictive density improves over deterministic ridge by ≥5% at the 20-step horizon; 95% predictive intervals are well-calibrated.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_false: Posterior std is approximately uniform across modes (priors are ignored); log predictive density matches or underperforms the deterministic baseline; predictive intervals are either over-narrow (posterior collapsed to MLE) or uniformly wide (no information gain).
hypotheses.risks: Variational inference may collapse to the MLE, making the hypothesis indistinguishable from a deterministic baseline; Laplace approximation may be inaccurate for the heavy-tailed tail. Mitigation: report both VI and Laplace approximations, and check whether the posterior has collapsed.
hypotheses.relation_to_existing_methods: Generalizes BOOTSTRAP_H1's deterministic linear operator family by replacing point estimate with a posterior. Conceptually adjacent to probabilistic DMD / probabilistic Koopman, but implemented purely in latent space and requires no exogenous parameters or physical fields — fitting the current capability profile.
hypotheses.novelty_status: Novel in this project. Hierarchical shrinkage priors on eigenvalues indexed by POD mode energy is an unconventional combination not standard in DMD / probabilistic Koopman literature and has not been proposed in any prior cycle.

hypotheses.name: POD-energy-band-structured sparse latent linear operator
hypotheses.scientific_question: Does enforcing a banded/sparse structural prior on the latent linear operator A — with sparsity pattern and bandwidth chosen to respect the energy hierarchy of the underlying POD basis — improve long-horizon predictive skill on development_validation relative to a fully dense ridge-regression operator at matched regularization strength?
hypotheses.mechanism: POD modes are ordered by decreasing reconstruction energy. In many CFD latent reductions, dominant modes couple mostly among themselves and to a small neighborhood of weaker modes; low-energy tail modes couple to a small set of head modes rather than to each other. The hypothesis: an A whose block structure reflects this coupling — dense within the high-energy block, low-rank for tail-to-head, sparse within the tail — should generalize better than a dense A with many free parameters that overfit low-energy cross-couplings. The structural prior is a compression of domain knowledge about POD's energy ordering into the operator's geometry.
hypotheses.mathematical_form: Partition z = [z_H; z_T] with z_H ∈ R^K (top-K high-energy modes) and z_T ∈ R^{52-K} (tail). Decompose A = [[A_{HH}, A_{HL}], [A_{LH}, A_{LL}]]. Structure: A_{HH} ∈ R^{K×K} dense; A_{HL} ∈ R^{K×(52-K)} banded of bandwidth w_H; A_{LH} ∈ R^{(52-K)×K} low-rank of rank r_L; A_{LL} ∈ R^{(52-K)×(52-K)} sparse with fraction f_L of entries. Loss: minimize Σ_t ||A z_t − z_{t+1}||² + λ ||A||_F² + μ_bandwidth ||bandmask||². Total free parameters ≪ dense ridge (52² ≈ 2704).
hypotheses.motivation: The dense ridge operator used in BOOTSTRAP_H1 is known to smear energy across poorly observed directions and overfit cross-couplings that are statistical artifacts. Sparsity and low-rank constraints are well established in compressed-sensing system identification, but the specific 'POD-energy-respecting' structure (dense head–head, banded head–tail, low-rank tail–head, sparse tail–tail) has not been tested here. If the structure is correct, this gives both better generalization and interpretable mode-coupling diagnostics that the dense baseline cannot provide.
hypotheses.explanation_of_previous_failure: C001_H01 (delay-coordinate), C001_H03 (slow-manifold/fast-fluctuation), and C002_H02 (regime-aware Koopman) all involved variants of linear operators but failed infrastructurally (run() signature, smoke-test contract). The mechanisms were never tested. C003_H02 introduces a structural sparsity prior that none of those attempts considered; it is a fresh scientific mechanism, not a re-parameterization. It also avoids the C002_H03 failure mode by using only latent_state/latent_history and by keeping normalization on development-only splits.
hypotheses.distinguishing_prediction: If the energy-band structure is correct: (a) the structured A achieves lower 20-step validation MSE than a dense ridge baseline despite having strictly fewer free parameters; (b) the learned coupling pattern is qualitatively aligned with the energy hierarchy — strongest couplings within the top-K block, weaker cross-block, weakest within the tail; (c) most prediction error originates from the low-energy tail modes, not from systematic drift in the top-K modes (i.e., the linear core captures the dominant dynamics).
hypotheses.minimum_experiment: Train on development_train with K ∈ {8, 16, 24}, bandwidth w_H ∈ {3, 5, full}, low-rank r_L ∈ {2, 4, 8}, tail sparsity f_L ∈ {0.1, 0.3, 0.5}. Compare against a dense ridge baseline with matched λ. Evaluate on development_validation: 1-step MSE, 20-step MSE, 100-step MSE; per-block (z_H, z_T) MSE separately; parameter count; eigenvalue spectrum of A; learned coupling-pattern visualization. Pass research_dir and output_dir to AlgorithmAgent.run() to avoid the C001_* missing-args failure; declare latent_dim=52 in the contract to avoid the C002_* smoke-test contract mismatch. Falsification criterion: if no (K, w_H, r_L, f_L) setting beats dense ridge on 20-step validation MSE by ≥5% AND the learned coupling pattern shows no qualitative stratification by energy block, the POD-energy-band-structure mechanism is rejected.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_true: 20-step validation MSE < dense-ridge MSE by ≥5%; eigenvalue spectrum of A shows clean separation between dominant and suppressed modes; the coupling pattern looks like a small graph with edges concentrated in the top-K block.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_false: Structured A underperforms dense ridge at every tested setting; the learned A is essentially dense and shows no energy-block stratification; the eigenvalue spectrum is indistinguishable from dense ridge.
hypotheses.risks: If the true dynamics couple high- and low-energy modes strongly (e.g., via nonlinearity), the banded/sparse constraint may be too restrictive. Mitigation: include a 'fully dense within each block, structured only across blocks' control, which removes the within-block sparsity but keeps the cross-block low-rank/banded structure.
hypotheses.relation_to_existing_methods: Block-sparse Koopman and banded operator learning exist in the system-identification literature, but the specific POD-energy-respecting pattern (dense head–head, banded head–tail, low-rank tail–head, sparse tail–tail) and its falsifiable alignment with the energy hierarchy is novel within this project. SINDy-style sparse regression is related in spirit but requires physical-state variables (divergence/curl) that are unavailable here; this hypothesis works purely in latent space.
hypotheses.novelty_status: Novel in this project. The 'POD-energy-band' structural prior on A has not been proposed in any prior cycle and, to my knowledge, is not standard in Koopman-on-CFD literature.

hypotheses.name: Energy-decomposed linear core plus low-energy-tail residual correction
hypotheses.scientific_question: Is prediction error in the 52D latent space driven primarily by nonlinearity concentrated in the low-energy POD tail (modes K+1 to 52), so that restricting a nonlinear residual correction g(z) to that tail strictly improves over both a fully linear operator and a full-state nonlinear residual at matched parameter count?
hypotheses.mechanism: POD is L2-optimal, so the top-K modes carry most of the reconstruction energy; their dynamics are typically approximately linear because they correspond to coherent structures. The tail modes capture small-scale, intermittent, often nonlinear dynamics. The hypothesis decomposes the dynamics along the physically meaningful energy axis: a single linear A captures the full state; a small nonlinear residual g acts only on the tail and does not modify the high-energy block. This cleanly separates the linear and nonlinear contributions in a way that is falsifiable by a built-in control experiment (the same g applied to the high-energy block only).
hypotheses.mathematical_form: Split z = [z_H; z_T] with z_H ∈ R^K, z_T ∈ R^{52-K}. Linear core: [z_H^{t+1}; z_T^{t+1,lin}] = A [z_H^t; z_T^t] with A ∈ R^{52×52}. Nonlinear residual: g_θ: R^{52} → R^{52-K}, so z_T^{t+1} = z_T^{t+1,lin} + g_θ(z_t) and z_H^{t+1} = z_H^{t+1,lin} (residual does NOT modify z_H). Total: z^{t+1} = A z_t + [0; g_θ(z_t)]. For the full-state control, replace [0; g_θ] with g_full(z_t) ∈ R^{52}; for the high-energy control, use g_H(z_t) ∈ R^K in the top block.
hypotheses.motivation: Hybrid linear + nonlinear ROMs are common (linear Galerkin + neural correction), but the specific design choice of restricting the nonlinear correction to the low-energy tail — with the falsifiable prediction that the high-energy block needs no nonlinear correction — has not been tested. C001_H03 attempted a related idea (multi-scale slow manifold + fast fluctuation) but failed for the run() signature bug and was, in any case, a timescale-axis decomposition rather than an energy-axis one. C003_H03 is a fundamentally different mechanism, with a built-in negative-result arm.
hypotheses.explanation_of_previous_failure: C001_H03 (slow manifold / fast fluctuation) failed at run() signature, mechanism untested. C002_H03 (sparse symbolic with closure residual) failed at the contract validator (final-test access in representation.normalization). C003_H03 keeps a residual_operator but locates it in a specific energy-defined subspace and includes a built-in control (residual on the high-energy block only) that directly tests the energy-axis hypothesis. Normalization and data access are restricted to development_train and development_validation to avoid the C002_H03 contract failure, and the run() signature is fixed.
hypotheses.distinguishing_prediction: If the energy-decomposition mechanism is correct: (a) g_tail (acting only on z_T) achieves ≥90% of g_full's improvement over the linear baseline at matched parameter count; (b) adding the equivalent residual on the high-energy block g_H alone does not improve metrics significantly (<10% gain); (c) ||g(z_T)||_mean > 0 and scales monotonically with ||z_T||, indicating g is responding to real nonlinear content rather than producing noise.
hypotheses.minimum_experiment: Train three variants on development_train with K ∈ {12, 24, 36}: (i) A only (linear baseline); (ii) A + full-state residual g_full (g_full: R^{52} → R^{52}); (iii) A + tail-only residual g_tail (g_tail: R^{52} → R^{52-K}); (iv) control: A + head-only residual g_H (g_H: R^{52} → R^K). Hold MLP width and depth constant across (ii), (iii), (iv). Evaluate on development_validation: 1-step MSE on z_H and z_T separately; 20-step MSE on z_H and z_T separately; ||g(z)|| mean and its correlation with ||z_T||; parameter count. Pass research_dir and output_dir to AlgorithmAgent.run(); declare latent_dim=52; restrict normalization to development_train and development_validation; avoid the special character that triggered the GBK UnicodeEncodeError in C002_H03. Falsification criterion: if g_tail achieves < 0.9 × g_full on 20-step MSE for all tested K AND adding g_H on the high-energy block improves 20-step MSE by ≥10%, the energy-decomposition mechanism is rejected (nonlinearity is broadly distributed, not tail-localized).
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_true: g_tail recovers ≥90% of g_full's gain; g_H alone does not improve 20-step MSE; ||g(z_T)|| scales monotonically with ||z_T||, and the correlation is statistically significant; most residual improvement comes from the tail block, not the head block.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_false: g_tail substantially underperforms g_full (energy restriction is too aggressive); g_H improves MSE by ≥10%; ||g(z_T)|| is uncorrelated with ||z_T||, indicating g is producing noise rather than responding to real nonlinear structure.
hypotheses.risks: If the POD latent is not strictly energy-separable in its dynamics (modes mix strongly), the tail restriction may discard critical nonlinear content. The control experiment g_H directly measures this risk; if g_H is informative, the hypothesis is wrong.
hypotheses.relation_to_existing_methods: Hybrid linear + nonlinear ROMs are standard, but the specific design choice — residual lives only in the low-energy tail, with a built-in negative-result arm on the high-energy block — has not been tested in prior cycles. Closest in spirit to scale-aware neural correction but with a falsifiable energy-axis spatial structure rather than a generic split.
hypotheses.novelty_status: Novel in this project. The 'residual restricted to the low-energy tail with a built-in high-energy control' design is a specific, falsifiable architectural choice that none of the prior hypotheses (C001_H03's slow-manifold/fast-fluctuation timescale split, C002_H03's symbolic-closure residual) considered. The control arm (g_H on the high-energy block) makes the falsification explicit and quantitative.
